questions.question: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Electric Generator**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electric Generator__ is a device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction.
 
• In an electric generator, a conductor (like a coil of wire) moves in a magnetic field to produce electricity.
 
• It works on the principle of electromagnetic induction, discovered by Michael Faraday.
 
• Generators are widely used for producing electricity in power plants, industrial facilities, and portable devices.
 
• They are essential in ensuring power supply during outages or in areas where electricity is not readily available.
 
• Unlike batteries, generators do not store energy but directly convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
 
• Generators can be powered by various energy sources such as steam, water, wind, or internal combustion engines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Battery:**

 
 
• A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy.
 
• It is used in portable electronic devices and vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motor: **
 
 
• An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• It is used in appliances like fans, washing machines, and industrial machinery.
 
 
 
• **Capacitor:**
 
 
• A capacitor stores electrical energy in an electric field.
 
• It is used in electronic circuits for energy storage, filtering, and signal processing.

questions.question: Which type of spherical mirror is used by dentists to see a large image of the teeth of patients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Concave mirror** is the type of spherical mirror used by **dentists** to see a **large (magnified) image** of a patient's teeth.
 
• The core logic lies in the image formation properties of a concave mirror: when an object is placed very close to the mirror (between the **pole** and the **principal focus**), the resulting image is **virtual**, **erect**, and **magnified**.
 
• **Plane mirrors** are incorrect because they produce an image that is the **same size** as the object, providing no magnification for detailed dental work.
 
• **Convex mirrors** are incorrect because they always produce a **diminished** (smaller) image, which would make it harder for a dentist to see details.
 
• **Bifocal mirrors** is not a standard term in optics; **bifocal lenses** are used in spectacles to correct vision, not for magnification in dental tools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave mirrors** are also widely used in **shaving mirrors** and **makeup mirrors** to provide a clear, enlarged view of the face.
 
• They are used in **torches**, **searchlights**, and **vehicle headlights** to produce a powerful parallel beam of light when the light source is placed at the focus.
 
• **Convex mirrors** are commonly used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they give a **wider field of view**, allowing drivers to see a large area of traffic behind them.
 
• A **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is curved inwards (towards the center of the sphere) is a **concave mirror**, while one curved outwards is a **convex mirror**.

questions.question: According to Ohm's Law, if the resistance of a conductor is doubled while the potential difference remains constant, the current will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Halved**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** defines the relationship between **voltage**, **current**, and **resistance** in an electrical circuit, stating that the **current** passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the **potential difference** across the two points.
 
• The mathematical formula for **Ohm’s Law** is **V = IR**, where **V** is the **potential difference**, **I** is the **current**, and **R** is the **resistance** of the conductor.
 
• From the formula **I = V / R**, it is clear that **current (I)** is **inversely proportional** to **resistance (R)** when the **potential difference (V)** remains **constant**.
 
• If the **resistance** of the conductor is **doubled** (i.e., new resistance **R' = 2R**) while **V** remains unchanged, the new current **I'** becomes **V / 2R**, which is exactly **half** of the original current. Thus, the current is **Halved**.
 
• This fundamental principle was discovered by the **German** physicist **Georg Simon Ohm** and published in his **1827** treatise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current**: It is defined as the **rate of flow of electric charge** through a cross-section of a conductor. Its **SI unit** is the **Ampere (A)**, named after **André-Marie Ampère**. One **Ampere** is equal to the flow of one **Coulomb** of charge per **second**.
 
• **Potential Difference (Voltage)**: This is the **work done** to move a unit charge from one point to another in an **electrical circuit**. Its **SI unit** is the **Volt (V)**. It provides the "pressure" that pushes the **electrons** through the circuit.
 
• **Electrical Resistance**: It is the property of a material to **oppose** the flow of **electric current**. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**. Resistance depends on several **physical factors** such as the **nature of the material**, **length**, **area of cross-section**, and **temperature**.
 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Conductors**: Materials that obey **Ohm's Law** (where the **V-I graph** is a **straight line** passing through the origin) are called **Ohmic conductors**, such as **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum**. Materials like **semiconductors**, **diodes**, and **transistors** do not follow this linear relationship and are called **non-Ohmic conductors**.
 
• **Conductance**: This is the **reciprocal of resistance** and represents the ease with which **current** flows through a conductor. Its **SI unit** is the **Siemens (S)** or **mho**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**:

 
 
• **Length**: Resistance is **directly proportional** to the **length** of the conductor. Doubling the length **doubles** the resistance.
 
• **Area of Cross-section**: Resistance is **inversely proportional** to the **cross-sectional area**. A **thicker wire** has **less resistance** than a **thinner wire** of the same material.
 
• **Resistivity**: This is an **intrinsic property** of the material. Conductors like **metals** have **low resistivity** (ranging from **10^-8 Ωm to 10^-6 Ωm**), while **insulators** like **rubber** have **high resistivity** (ranging from **10^12 to 10^17 Ωm**).
 
• **Temperature**: For most **metallic conductors**, resistance **increases** with an **increase in temperature** because of the increased **vibration of atoms**, which hinders the flow of **electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Applications**: **Ohm's Law** is used to design **electronic components** like **resistors**, **potentiometers**, and **rheostats** (variable resistors) used in **radios**, **heaters**, and **industrial machinery** to control the **magnitude of current**.

questions.question: Which statement best explains the higher energy content of fats compared to carbohydrates?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Fats have more carbon-hydrogen bonds__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Higher energy content in fats__**

 __
 
• Fats contain a greater number of **carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds__** compared to carbohydrates.
 
• When these bonds are broken during metabolism, they release a significant amount of **__energy__** in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
 
 
• **__Energy density of fats__**
 __
 
• Fats provide approximately **9 kilocalories per gram__**, while carbohydrates provide only about **__4 kilocalories per gram__**.
 
• This difference is due to the higher ratio of energy-rich **__C-H bonds__** in fats.
 
 
 
• **__Oxidation process__**
 __
 
• During oxidation, fats undergo a more extensive breakdown, releasing more energy compared to carbohydrates, which have fewer **C-H bonds__**.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Structure of fats__**

 __
 
• Fats are composed of **triglycerides__**, which consist of three fatty acid chains attached to a glycerol backbone.
 
• The fatty acid chains are long hydrocarbon chains, rich in **__C-H bonds__**, making them energy-dense.
 
 
 
• **__Structure of carbohydrates__**
 __
 
• Carbohydrates contain a higher proportion of **oxygen__** atoms and fewer **__C-H bonds__**, leading to less energy release upon oxidation.
 
• Examples include glucose and starch, which are readily utilized for short-term energy needs.
 
 
 
• **__Biological significance__**
 
 
• Fats serve as a long-term energy storage molecule, while carbohydrates are used for immediate energy requirements.
 
• The energy released from fat metabolism is critical for activities requiring sustained energy, such as endurance exercises.

questions.question: If, while calculating a planetary orbit, the value of the universal gravitational constant (G) is mistakenly taken as ten times its actual value, what effect will this have on the calculated gravitational force between the planet and the Sun?

options.text: The calculated force will remain unchanged.
The calculated force will be ten times less than the actual value.
The calculated force will be ten times greater than the actual value.
The calculated force will be half of the actual value.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The calculated force will be ten times greater than the actual value**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, the force of attraction between any two masses in the universe is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. The formula is expressed as **F = G (m1m2 / r2)**.
 
• In this equation, **G** represents the **Universal Gravitational Constant**. It acts as the scaling factor that determines the strength of the gravitational pull. Since **F** is in the numerator and **G** is also a multiplier in the numerator, the force **F** is **directly proportional** to **G**.
 
• If a scientist or student mistakenly takes the value of **G** as **10 times** its actual value (i.e., **10G** instead of **G**), the new force **F'** would be calculated as **F' = (10G) (m1m2 / r2)**.
 
• Mathematically, this results in **F' = 10 × F**. This means the calculated gravitational force will be exactly **ten times greater** than the true physical force existing between the **Sun** and the **planet**. *Hence, the statement regarding the tenfold increase in force is correct.*
 
• This linear relationship implies that any percentage error in the constant **G** will result in the same percentage error in the calculated force **F**, provided the **masses** and **distance** remain constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**: It is an empirical physical constant used in the calculation of gravitational effects. The currently accepted value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg²**.
 
• **Historical Context**: While **Sir Isaac Newton** introduced the law of gravitation in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**, he did not determine the value of **G**. It was **Henry Cavendish** who first measured the value of **G** in **1798** using a **torsion balance** experiment.
 
• **Distinction between G and g**: It is important to distinguish **G** from **g**, which is the **acceleration due to gravity**. While **G** is a **universal constant** that remains the same everywhere in the **universe**, **g** is a **vector quantity** that varies depending on the **location**, such as being **9.8 m/s²** on **Earth** but roughly **1.6 m/s²** on the **Moon**.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**: The gravitational force follows the **inverse square law**, meaning if the distance **r** between the **Sun** and the **planet** is doubled, the force becomes **one-fourth (1/4)** of its original value. This is a fundamental feature of **central forces**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensions of G**: The dimensional formula for the **Universal Gravitational Constant** is derived from the force equation as **[M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]**.
 
• **Nature of Gravitational Force**: It is the **weakest** of the four **fundamental forces** of nature (the others being **electromagnetism**, **strong nuclear force**, and **weak nuclear force**), yet it is the dominant force on **astronomical scales**.
 
• **Applications**: The value of **G** is critical in **Astrophysics** and **Cosmology** for determining the **mass of planets**, the **orbits of satellites**, and the **expansion rate of the universe**.
 
• **Standard Units**: In the **SI system**, the force is measured in **Newtons (N)**, mass in **kilograms (kg)**, and distance in **meters (m)**. Using incorrect units or values for **G** leads to massive discrepancies in **orbital mechanics** calculations.

questions.question: _______ are the most abundant cells in blood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Erythrocytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Erythrocytes **are the **most abundant cells** in the blood.
 
• **Blood** is a body fluid in humans and other animals that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells and metabolic waste products away from those same cells.
 
• Invertebrates, it is composed of **blood cells suspended in blood plasma.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

**Types of blood cells:**

**Red blood cells (RBCs or Erythrocytes):**

 
• It is the **most common type of blood cell.**
 
• Nearly **half of the blood's volume (40% to 45%) **is red blood cells.
 
• Adult humans have **roughly 20–30 trillion red blood cells** at any given time.
 
• The blood's red color is due to the spectral properties of the **hemic iron** ions in hemoglobin.
 
• The cells develop in the **bone marrow.**
 
• The normal life span of an RBC is about **100–120 days.**

**blood cells (WBCs or Leukocytes):**

 
• These are the cells of the immune system that are involved in **protecting the body against both infectious disease and foreign bodies.**
 
• These are found throughout the body, including the **blood and lymphatic system.**
 
• **These can further be classified into- **
 
 
• Neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes.
 
 

**Platelets (Thrombocytes):**

 
• These are blood components whose function is to help in the **clotting of blood.**
 
• **Low platelet concentration** is called **thrombocytopenia**.
 
• **Elevated platelet concentration** is called **thrombocytosis.**
 
• **Platelets** have a central role in **innate immunity**, directly binding pathogens and even destroying them.

questions.question: During free fall, when an object is released from rest, how does the gravitational force of the Earth affect its motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases the object's velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Free fall** is defined as the motion of an object where **gravity** is the only force acting upon it. When an object is released from **rest**, its **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**.
 
• The **gravitational force** of the Earth acts continuously on the object in the downward direction, causing it to **accelerate**. This constant acceleration is known as the **acceleration due to gravity**, denoted by **'g'**.
 
• Near the surface of the Earth, the value of **'g'** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. This means that for every **second** the object falls, its **velocity** increases by **9.8 m/s**.
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion** (**F = ma**), the force applied to the object's **mass** produces an acceleration in the same direction as the force. Since the **gravitational force** pulls the object toward the **Earth's center**, the object speeds up as it descends. *Hence, the statement that it increases the object's velocity is correct.*
 
• The statement that it decreases velocity is incorrect because a decrease in velocity would require an **upward force** (retardation) greater than the downward force. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• The statement that it maintains the object's velocity is incorrect because, according to **Newton's First Law**, velocity remains constant only if the **net external force** is **zero**. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• The statement that it stops the object instantly is incorrect as gravity is an **accelerating force**, not a resistive one like friction or a physical barrier. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** Its value is not constant everywhere on Earth. It is **maximum at the poles** and **minimum at the equator** due to the **oblate spheroid** shape of the Earth and the effect of **centrifugal force** caused by rotation.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight:** **Mass** is the amount of matter in an object and remains constant regardless of **location**. **Weight** is the **gravitational force** acting on that mass (**W = mg**). Therefore, an object's weight changes if the value of **'g'** changes (e.g., on the **Moon**, where **g** is about **1/6th** of Earth's).
 
• **Equations of Motion for Free Fall:** When an object falls under gravity from rest, the standard equations are modified: **v = gt**, **h = 1/2 gt²**, and **v² = 2gh**, where **v** is final velocity, **g** is **9.8 m/s²**, **t** is **time** in seconds, and **h** is the **height** or displacement.
 
• **Galileo's Observation:** In the late **16th century**, **Galileo Galilei** demonstrated that in a **vacuum** (absence of **air resistance**), all objects, regardless of their **mass**, fall with the same **acceleration**. This was famously illustrated by dropping two spheres of different masses from the **Leaning Tower of Pisa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Terminal Velocity:** In a real-world scenario with an **atmosphere**, an object will not increase its velocity indefinitely. As the velocity increases, the **air resistance** (drag) also increases. Eventually, the upward air resistance equals the downward weight, the **net force** becomes **zero**, and the object continues at a constant speed called **terminal velocity**.
 
• **Universal Law of Gravitation:** This force is governed by **Sir Isaac Newton's** law formulated in **1687**, which states that the force is **directly proportional** to the product of the **masses** and **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** between them (**F = G m1m2 / r²**).
 
• **Energy Transformation:** During free fall, **Potential Energy (PE = mgh)** is progressively converted into **Kinetic Energy (KE = 1/2 mv²)**. According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, the total mechanical energy remains constant if air friction is ignored.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a paramagnetic material that is weakly attracted to an external magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Paramagnetic materials** are substances that are **weakly attracted** by an external magnetic field and move from a weaker to a stronger part of the field.
 
• These materials possess atoms or molecules with a **permanent magnetic dipole moment**, which is primarily due to the presence of **unpaired electrons**.
 
• In the presence of an external field, these atomic dipoles align themselves **parallel** to the direction of the field, resulting in a weak net magnetization.
 
• **Aluminium** is a classic example of a paramagnetic material; other examples include **platinum**, **magnesium**, **lithium**, and **manganese**.
 
• The **magnetic susceptibility** of paramagnetic substances is a **small positive value**, meaning they are only slightly magnetized.
 
• The **relative permeability** (μᵣ) of these substances is slightly **greater than 1**.
 
• The magnetization of these materials is temporary and disappears as soon as the external magnetic field is removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Ferromagnetic materials:** Substances like **Iron**, cobalt, and nickel are **strongly attracted** to magnetic fields and can retain their magnetization even after the field is removed.
 
• **Diamagnetic materials:** Substances like **Copper**, **Lead**, gold, and water are **weakly repelled** by an external magnetic field and have a small negative magnetic susceptibility.
 
• **Curie Law:** For paramagnetic materials, the intensity of magnetization is **inversely proportional** to the absolute temperature, meaning their magnetic properties decrease as temperature increases.

questions.question:
**Consider the following statements about the 'Dispersion of Light':**

 
• 
 
It is the splitting of white light into its constituent seven colors.

 
 
• 
 
Red light deviates the most, while Violet deviates the least.

 
 
• 
 
A Rainbow is a natural phenomenon caused by dispersion, refraction, and total internal reflection.

 

**Select the correct code:**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dispersion of Light** is defined as the phenomenon of splitting a beam of **white light** into its constituent **seven colors** (VIBGYOR) when it passes through a transparent medium like a **glass prism**. This happens because different colors of light travel at **different speeds** in a medium, causing them to bend by different angles. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The degree of bending or **deviation** depends on the **wavelength** of the light. According to **Cauchy's formula**, the refractive index of a medium is inversely proportional to the wavelength. **Red light** has the **longest wavelength** in the visible spectrum and travels the fastest in the medium, resulting in the **least deviation**. Conversely, **Violet light** has the **shortest wavelength** and travels the slowest, leading to the **most deviation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A **Rainbow** is a spectacular natural phenomenon caused by the **dispersion** of sunlight by tiny **water droplets** present in the atmosphere after rain. The process involves three main steps: **Refraction** of sunlight as it enters the drop, **Dispersion** into seven colors, **Total Internal Reflection** at the back of the droplet, and finally, **Refraction** again as it exits the drop toward the observer's eye. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The sequence of colors formed during dispersion is represented by the acronym **VIBGYOR**, which stands for **Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red**. This discovery was famously demonstrated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in the year **1666** using a glass prism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Visible Spectrum:** The range of wavelengths that the human eye can perceive is approximately **400 nm to 700 nm**. **Violet** is at the lower end (approx **400 nm**) while **Red** is at the upper end (approx **700 nm**).
 
• **Refractive Index:** It is a **dimensionless number** that describes how fast light travels through a medium compared to a vacuum. For a given medium, the **refractive index** is higher for **shorter wavelengths** (violet) and lower for **longer wavelengths** (red).
 
• **Spectrum:** The band of seven colors obtained on a screen when white light passes through a prism is called a **spectrum**. Light that consists of only one color or wavelength is called **monochromatic light**, while light like sunlight is **polychromatic**.
 
• **Total Internal Reflection (TIR):** For TIR to occur in a rainbow, the light must strike the inner surface of the raindrop at an angle greater than the **critical angle**. This ensures the light stays within the drop to be dispersed effectively before reaching the viewer.
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction:** Apart from rainbows, the atmosphere causes other optical phenomena like the **twinkling of stars** and **advanced sunrise/delayed sunset**, though these are distinct from the process of dispersion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Primary vs. Secondary Rainbows:** A **Primary Rainbow** is formed by **one internal reflection** inside the raindrop, showing Red on the outside and Violet on the inside. A **Secondary Rainbow** is formed by **two internal reflections**, resulting in a fainter appearance and **reversed colors** (Violet on the outside).
 
• **Recombination of Spectrum:** **Newton** also showed that if a second identical prism is placed in an **inverted position** behind the first prism, the seven colors **recombine** to form **white light** again.
 
• **Angular Dispersion:** The difference in the **angle of deviation** between the extreme colors (Violet and Red) is known as **angular dispersion**, which determines the width of the spectrum formed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main component of 'CNG' (Compressed Natural Gas)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)** is an eco-friendly alternative to conventional fossil fuels like petrol and diesel. It is produced by compressing natural gas to less than **1%** of its standard atmospheric volume.
 
• The primary and most significant component of **CNG** is **Methane (CH4)**, which typically constitutes about **80% to 95%** of the total gas mixture. ***Hence, the statement identifying Methane as the main component is correct.***
 
• **Ethane (C2H6)** is a secondary constituent found in natural gas, usually ranging from **1% to 6%** depending on the source. While it contributes to the energy content, it is not the dominant component. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Propane (C3H8)** and **Butane (C4H10)** are present in trace amounts in **CNG**, but they are the primary components of **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)**. Because they are found in very low concentrations in **CNG**, they are not considered main components. ***Hence, these statements are incorrect.***
 
• The compression process for **CNG** involves storage at high pressures, typically between **200 and 250 bars** (approximately **3,000 to 3,600 psi**), to ensure efficient storage in cylindrical tanks within **vehicles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Characteristics of Methane:** **Methane** is the simplest **hydrocarbon**, consisting of **one carbon atom** and **four hydrogen atoms**. It is **colorless, odorless**, and **tasteless** in its pure form. For safety, a pungent odorant like **Ethyl Mercaptan** is added to detect leaks.
 
• **Environmental Benefits:** **CNG** is considered a "green fuel" because its combustion produces significantly lower levels of harmful pollutants. It reduces **Carbon Monoxide (CO)** emissions by roughly **80%** and **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)** by nearly **50%** compared to traditional fuels.
 
• **Storage and Safety:** **CNG** has a narrow flammability range (**5% to 15%** in air) and a high **auto-ignition temperature** of approximately **540°C**. Since it is **lighter than air**, it disperses rapidly into the atmosphere in case of a leak, making it safer than **LPG** which is heavier and tends to pool on the ground.
 
• **Applications and Usage:** It is widely used in the **transportation sector**, particularly for **Public Transport** such as buses, auto-rickshaws, and taxis. In **India**, **New Delhi** became one of the first major cities to mandate **CNG** for its public transport fleet in the **year 1998** following Supreme Court directives to control **air pollution**.
 
• **Comparison with LPG:** While **CNG** is primarily **Methane**, **LPG** is a mixture of **Propane** and **Butane**. **CNG** remains in a gaseous state under high pressure, whereas **LPG** turns into a liquid under relatively lower pressure (approx **7-8 bars**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fuel Efficiency:** **CNG** offers a high **octane rating** of about **120-130**, which prevents engine knocking and allows for higher compression ratios in **Internal Combustion Engines (ICE)**.
 
• **India's Initiatives:** The Government of India, under the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**, has aggressively expanded the **City Gas Distribution (CGD)** network. Major companies like **GAIL (India) Limited** and **Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL)** are key players in the distribution of **CNG**.
 
• **Global Context:** Countries like **Iran, China, Pakistan, and Argentina** are among the leading users of **Natural Gas Vehicles (NGVs)** globally due to the abundance of natural gas reserves and the lower cost of **Methane** relative to crude oil derivatives.
 
• **Economic Impact:** **CNG** is generally **30% to 50%** cheaper than petrol or diesel in terms of **running cost per kilometer**, making it a preferred choice for high-mileage commercial vehicle operators.

questions.question: Which of the following is the sweetest sugar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fructose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fructose**, also known as **fruit sugar**, is a simple **monosaccharide** found in many plants, where it is often bonded to glucose to form the disaccharide sucrose.
 
• It is the **sweetest of all naturally occurring sugars**. On a relative sweetness scale where **sucrose** (table sugar) is ranked at **100**, **fructose** scores approximately **173**.
 
• Chemically, it is a **ketohexose** with the formula **C6H12O6**. It is a **functional isomer** of glucose, meaning they share the same molecular formula but have different structural arrangements (fructose has a ketone group, while glucose has an aldehyde group).
 
• It is highly **soluble in water** and is found in high concentrations in **honey**, **tree fruits**, **berries**, and **root vegetables**.
 
• Due to its high sweetness, it is often used commercially in the form of **High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS)** in the food industry to enhance flavor and shelf-life in processed goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sucrose:**

 
 
• It is a **disaccharide** composed of one unit of **glucose** and one unit of **fructose** linked by an **alpha-1,2-glycosidic bond**.
 
• Commonly known as **table sugar**, it is extracted primarily from **sugar cane** and **sugar beet**.
 
• It serves as the **standard reference** for measuring the sweetness of other substances.
 
 
 
• **Glucose:**
 
 
• It is a **monosaccharide** (aldohexose) and is the **primary source of energy** for living organisms.
 
• It is also known as **blood sugar** or **dextrose**.
 
• Its relative sweetness is approximately **74**, making it significantly less sweet than fructose.
 
 
 
• **Maltose:**
 
 
• It is a **disaccharide** formed from two units of **glucose** joined by an **alpha-1,4-bond**.
 
• Commonly called **malt sugar**, it is found in **germinating cereals** like barley and is a product of **starch digestion**.
 
• It is the **least sweet** among the options provided, with a relative sweetness score of about **32**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relative Sweetness Scale:** The perceived sweetness of sugars is compared against sucrose. For instance, **Lactose** (milk sugar) has the lowest sweetness among common sugars, rated at about **16**.
 
• **Physical Properties:** **Fructose** is the most **hygroscopic** (water-absorbing) of all sugars, which helps in maintaining moisture in baked goods.
 
• **Metabolism:** Unlike glucose, which is processed throughout the body, **fructose** is metabolized almost entirely in the **liver**.
 
• **Date of Discovery:** Fructose was discovered by **Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut** in **1847**.

questions.question: Which of the following is strongest oxidising agent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Among the given options, **Fluorine (F₂)** is the strongest **oxidizing agent**. An oxidizing agent is a substance that has the ability to **oxidize** other substances, meaning it accepts electrons easily.
 
• The strength of an oxidizing agent is measured by its **Standard Reduction Potential (E°)**. **Fluorine** has the highest positive reduction potential of **+2.87 V** in the entire periodic table, making it the most powerful oxidizer.
 
• **Chlorine (Cl₂)** has a reduction potential of **+1.36 V**. While it is a strong oxidizing agent, it is significantly weaker than **Fluorine**.
 
• **Bromine (Br₂)** and **Iodine (I₂)** have reduction potentials of **+1.09 V** and **+0.54 V** respectively. This demonstrates a clear trend where the oxidizing power **decreases** as we move down **Group 17** of the periodic table.
 
• The order of oxidizing power for the halogens is **F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors affecting Oxidizing Power:** The oxidizing strength of halogens in aqueous solution depends on three main energy factors: **Bond Dissociation Enthalpy**, **Electron Gain Enthalpy**, and **Hydration Enthalpy**.

 
 
• **Low Bond Dissociation Enthalpy:** The **F-F bond** is surprisingly weak due to the high inter-electronic repulsion between the lone pairs on the small **Fluorine atoms**.
 
• **High Hydration Enthalpy:** The **Fluoride ion (F⁻)** is very small, which leads to a very high **hydration enthalpy** when it is surrounded by water molecules. This strongly favors the reduction of **F₂** to **F⁻**.
 
 
 
• **Electronegativity:** **Fluorine** is the most **electronegative** element in the periodic table with a value of **4.0** on the **Pauling scale**. This reflects its intense tendency to attract shared pairs of electrons.
 
• **Physical States:** Under standard conditions, **Fluorine** and **Chlorine** are gases, **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid, and **Iodine** is a shiny violet-black solid. This change in physical state is due to the increase in **Van der Waals forces** as the size of the **halogen atoms** increases down the group.
 
• **Atomic Number and Electronic Configuration:** **Fluorine** has the **atomic number 9** and an electronic configuration of **[He] 2s² 2p⁵**. It needs only one electron to achieve the stable **noble gas configuration** of Neon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• It is a common misconception that **Chlorine** should be a stronger oxidizer because it has a more negative **Electron Gain Enthalpy** than **Fluorine**. however, the **Standard Electrode Potential** considers the entire process of turning a molecule into a hydrated ion.
 
• Because **Fluorine** is such a strong oxidizing agent, it is extremely reactive and can even oxidize water to **Oxygen** or **Ozone**. It was first isolated by **Henri Moissan** in **1886**, for which he received the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1906**.
 
• **Uses:** **Fluorine compounds** are used in toothpaste (as **Fluoride** to prevent cavities), in the manufacture of **Teflon** (non-stick coating), and in the enrichment of **Uranium** for nuclear power.

questions.question: A 5 kg object experiences a gravitational force of about 49 N on Earth. This implies the value of g used is approximately:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __9.8 m/s²**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The gravitational force__ on an object is given by the formula F = m × g.
 
• Here, F = 49 N and m = 5 kg, so g = F/m = 49/5 = 9.8 m/s².
 
• This value of g corresponds to the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth.
 
• The acceleration due to gravity varies slightly depending on location but is commonly approximated as 9.8 m/s².
 
• This value is used to calculate gravitational force in various physics problems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration due to gravity:**

 
 
• It is the rate of increase of velocity of an object due to the Earth's gravitational force.
 
• It is denoted by g and has a standard value of 9.8 m/s².
 
 
 
• **Variation of g:**
 
 
• g decreases with altitude and increases towards the poles due to the Earth's shape.
 
• It also depends on the density of the Earth's crust in the location.
 
 
 
• **Weight of an object:**
 
 
• Weight is the product of mass (m) and acceleration due to gravity (g).
 
• It is a force and is measured in newtons (N).

questions.question: Identify the 'Natural Polymer' among the following:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cellulose** is the most abundant **natural polymer** found on **Earth**. It is a **complex carbohydrate** or **polysaccharide** consisting of **3,000** or more **glucose units**. It forms the primary structural component of the **cell wall** of green **plants** and many forms of **algae**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Cellulose is correct.***
 
• **Nylon** is a generic designation for a family of **synthetic polymers** known as **polyamides**. It was first produced on **February 28, 1935**, by **Wallace Carothers** at **DuPont’s** research facility. It is entirely **man-made** from **petrochemicals** and does not occur in nature. ***Hence, the statement regarding Nylon is incorrect.***
 
• **Terylene** is a **synthetic polyester** fiber produced by the **polymerizing** of **ethylene glycol** and **terephthalic acid**. It is widely used in the **textile industry** to make **clothing**, **sheets**, and **sails** due to its **elasticity** and **resistance** to friction. ***Hence, the statement regarding Terylene is incorrect.***
 
• **PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride)** is the world's third-most widely produced **synthetic plastic** polymer. It is created through the **polymerization** of the **vinyl chloride monomer**. It is extensively used in **construction** for **pipes**, **windows**, and **doors**. ***Hence, the statement regarding PVC is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Polymers:** **Polymers** are classified based on their **source** into three categories: **Natural**, **Semi-synthetic**, and **Synthetic**. **Natural polymers** are found in **plants** and **animals**, such as **proteins**, **starch**, and **cellulose**.
 
• **Examples of Natural Polymers:**
 
 
• **Starch:** A **polymer** of **glucose** found in **potatoes**, **rice**, and **wheat**.
 
• **Proteins:** These are **polymers** of **amino acids** and are essential for **growth** and **repair** in living organisms.
 
• **Natural Rubber:** Obtained from the **latex** of **Hevea brasiliensis** trees, it is a **polymer** of **isoprene** (**2-methyl-1,3-butadiene**).
 
 
 
• **Semi-synthetic Polymers:** These are derived from **natural polymers** through **chemical modification**. A common example is **Rayon** (**Viscose**), which is chemically treated **cellulose** used to make **fabrics** that resemble **silk**.
 
• **Synthetic Polymers:** These are **man-made** polymers designed for specific industrial and domestic **applications**. Examples include **Polyethylene** (used in **bags**), **Bakelite** (used in **electrical switches**), and **Teflon** (used in **non-stick cookware**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biodegradability:** Most **natural polymers** like **Cellulose** and **Starch** are **biodegradable**, meaning they can be broken down by **microorganisms** in the **environment**. In contrast, **synthetic polymers** like **PVC** and **Nylon** are generally **non-biodegradable** and contribute to **environmental pollution**.
 
• **Composition of Wood:** **Wood** is one of the most common sources of **cellulose**, containing approximately **40% to 50%** cellulose, while **cotton fiber** contains nearly **90%**.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** **Cellulose** is the primary **raw material** for the **paper industry**. It is also used to produce **cellophane**, **explosives** (**nitrocellulose**), and **thickening agents** in the **food industry**.
 
• **Polymerization:** This is the **chemical process** of reacting **monomer** molecules together in a **chemical reaction** to form **polymer chains**. **Synthetic polymers** are created through **addition polymerization** or **condensation polymerization**.

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched with its cofactor?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Nitrogenase — Mo__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Nitrogenase__**

 __
 
• Nitrogenase is a key enzyme involved in biological nitrogen fixation, converting atmospheric **N₂__** into ammonia (**__NH₃__**).
 
• The enzyme contains **__Molybdenum (Mo)__** as a cofactor, which plays a critical role in electron transfer during the reaction.
 
• Molybdenum is part of the **__Fe-Mo cofactor__** (FeMo-co), which is essential for the enzyme's catalytic activity.
 
• This enzyme is found in nitrogen-fixing microorganisms such as **__Rhizobium__** and cyanobacteria.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Other enzyme-cofactor matches__**

 __
 
• **Carbonic anhydrase__**: Contains **__Zinc (Zn²⁺)__** as its cofactor, not **__Iron (Fe²⁺)__**.
 
• **__Salivary amylase__**: Uses **__Chloride ions__** as an activator, not **__Zinc (Zn²⁺)__**.
 
• **__Urease__**: Requires **__Nickel (Ni²⁺)__** as its cofactor, not **__Copper (Cu²⁺)__**.
 
 
 
• **__Importance of cofactors__**
 __
 
• Cofactors are non-protein chemical compounds or metallic ions that are required for an enzyme's biological activity.
 
• They can be **organic molecules__** (coenzymes) or **__inorganic ions__** (metal ions).
 
• Examples include **__Mg²⁺__** for DNA polymerase and **__Cu²⁺__** for cytochrome oxidase.

questions.question: In the presence of sunlight, chlorine is added to hydrocarbons in a very fast reaction. Chlorine can replace the hydrogen atoms one by one. It is called a/an __________ reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**substitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **substitution reaction** is a type of chemical process where one **atom** or functional group in a chemical compound is replaced by another atom or group. In the context of hydrocarbons, this typically involves the replacement of a **hydrogen atom**.
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**, also known as **alkanes** (such as **methane**, **ethane**, etc.), are generally quite unreactive under normal conditions because they consist of strong **C-C** and **C-H single bonds**.
 
• In the presence of **sunlight** or **ultraviolet (UV) light**, chlorine reacts with these hydrocarbons in a very fast reaction. The energy from the **UV radiation** is required to break the **Cl-Cl bond** to initiate the process.
 
• During this reaction, **chlorine** atoms replace the hydrogen atoms of the hydrocarbon one by one. This stepwise replacement continues until all the hydrogen atoms are substituted by chlorine atoms. *Hence, the statement describing this as a substitution reaction is correct.*
 
• For example, in the chlorination of **methane** (**CH₄**), the reaction produces **chloromethane** (**CH₃Cl**), then **dichloromethane** (**CH₂Cl₂**), then **trichloromethane** (**CHCl₃**), and finally **tetrachloromethane** (**CCl₄**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Addition Reaction**: Unlike substitution, an **addition reaction** occurs in **unsaturated hydrocarbons** (alkenes and alkynes) containing **double or triple bonds**. In this reaction, atoms are added across the multiple bond to convert it into a **single bond**. A common example is the **hydrogenation** of vegetable oils using a **nickel (Ni) catalyst** at a temperature of **200°C** to form solid fats.
 
• **Elimination Reaction**: This is the opposite of an addition reaction where two substituents are removed from a molecule, typically resulting in the formation of a **double bond**. For instance, the **dehydration of ethanol** using **concentrated sulphuric acid** (**H₂SO₄**) at **170°C** yields **ethene**.
 
• **Combustion Reaction**: Hydrocarbons react with **oxygen** to produce **carbon dioxide** (**CO₂**), **water** (**H₂O**), and **heat**. This is a highly **exothermic** reaction and is the primary principle behind the use of fossil fuels.
 
• **Oxidation**: Alcohols can be converted into **carboxylic acids** using oxidizing agents such as **alkaline potassium permanganate** (**KMnO₄**) or **acidified potassium dichromate** (**K₂Cr₂O₇**). For example, **ethanol** is oxidized to **ethanoic acid** (acetic acid).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Free Radical Mechanism**: The substitution of chlorine in alkanes follows a **free radical mechanism**. This involves three distinct stages: **initiation** (creation of Cl radicals), **propagation** (reaction of radicals with the hydrocarbon), and **termination** (radicals pairing up).
 
• **Reactivity of Halogens**: The rate of halogenation varies significantly. **Fluorine** (**F₂**) is the most reactive and can be explosive, while **Iodine** (**I₂**) is the least reactive, often requiring a **catalyst** or oxidizing agent to drive the reaction forward.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: These reactions are vital for producing **solvents** and chemical intermediates. **Chloroform** (**CHCl₃**) was famously used as an **anaesthetic** in the **19th century**, while **Carbon tetrachloride** (**CCl₄**) was used as a **fire extinguisher** and **cleaning agent**.
 
• **Environmental Relevance**: Halogenated hydrocarbons, particularly **Chlorofluorocarbons** (**CFCs**), were widely used as **refrigerants** until the **1980s** when it was discovered they contribute to **ozone layer depletion**, leading to the global **Montreal Protocol** agreement in **1987**.

questions.question: Which factor determines the amount of water reabsorbed during urine formation in the human kidney?

options.text: The specific type of food consumed daily on a regular basis
The overall physical size and measurable dimensions of the human kidney
The amount of excess water and dissolved waste substances excreted by the body
The level of oxygen present in the circulating blood throughout the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the amount of excess water and dissolved waste substances excreted by the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of **urine formation** involves three main steps: **glomerular filtration**, **reabsorption**, and **secretion**. The amount of water reabsorbed is a highly regulated **physiological function** to maintain **homeostasis**.
 
• **Reabsorption** occurs primarily in the **nephron**, which is the **functional unit** of the kidney. Nearly **99%** of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the **renal tubules**.
 
• The primary factor determining water reabsorption is the **amount of excess water** present in the body. If the body is **well-hydrated**, less water is reabsorbed, leading to **dilute urine**. If the body is **dehydrated**, more water is reabsorbed into the **bloodstream** to conserve fluid. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Another determining factor is the **quantity of dissolved waste**, such as **urea**, **uric acid**, and **salts**, that needs to be excreted. A higher concentration of these **solutes** requires a specific volume of water to remain in the **filtrate** for effective excretion. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **specific type of food** consumed daily might affect the **solute concentration** (like salt intake), but it is not the direct biological determinant of the reabsorption mechanism itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **physical size and dimensions** of the kidney do not fluctuate to determine the daily or hourly volume of water reabsorption; this is a **metabolic** and **hormonal** process. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **oxygen levels** are critical for the **metabolic activity** of kidney cells (ATP production for active transport), they do not serve as the sensory signal for the volume of water reabsorption. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH):** Also known as **Vasopressin**, this hormone is secreted by the **posterior pituitary gland**. It plays a **critical role** in water reabsorption by making the **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)** and **collecting duct** more permeable to water.
 
• **Osmoreceptors:** These are specialized cells located in the **hypothalamus** that monitor the **osmolarity** of the blood. When **blood volume** decreases or **ionic concentration** increases, these receptors trigger the release of **ADH**.
 
• **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT):** This segment is responsible for the **obligatory reabsorption** of water, where approximately **70-80%** of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed regardless of the body's hydration state.
 
• **Loop of Henle:** This structure utilizes a **countercurrent mechanism** to create an **osmotic gradient** in the **renal medulla**, which is essential for the concentration of urine.
 
• **Diabetes Insipidus:** A medical condition caused by the **deficiency of ADH** or the kidney's inability to respond to it, resulting in the failure of water reabsorption and the production of **large volumes** of dilute urine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selective Reabsorption:** Substances like **glucose** and **amino acids** are reabsorbed **100%** under normal physiological conditions via **active transport**, whereas water reabsorption can be **passive** (osmosis).
 
• **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR):** In a healthy adult, the **GFR** is approximately **125 ml/minute** or **180 liters per day**. However, the volume of urine released is only about **1.5 liters**, highlighting the **efficiency** of the reabsorption process.
 
• **Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS):** This complex **hormonal cascade** is activated during a fall in **glomerular blood pressure**. It leads to the release of **Aldosterone** from the **adrenal cortex**, which promotes **sodium and water reabsorption** to increase **blood pressure**.
